(SCCH-5), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION. 
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 25.02.2021 passed by Court of VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.2710/2019. This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy and meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal. Hence, the appellants seek for enhancement of compensation. 
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal. 
3. Brief facts of the case are as under; The claimant was riding a Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-EJ-4918 on 02.04.2019 from Begur towards Bommanahalli, when he reached Papaiahreddy NC: 2024:KHC:5384 building, a Tempo Traveler bearing registration No.KA-01- AG-8036 was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety, due to which, he lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the claimant's motor cycle. 
Due to the said impact, claimant sustained grievous injuries. Immediately, he was shifted to Kavya Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein, first aid treatment was given. Thereafter, to St.John's Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein, he was inpatient for a period of 17 days. It is also stated that the claimant was aged 37 years and working as a cloth merchant and earning an income of Rs.25,000/- per month. 
3.1 On service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appeared before the Court and he was placed ex-parte. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company appeared before the Court and filed statement of objection denying the claim of the claimant including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and sought for dismissal of the claim petition. 
NC: 2024:KHC:5384 3.2 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration. 
Chandrashekar N Shetty @ Chandrashekar vs Suresh Kumar C on 8 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52045495/
2 3.3 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1, Doctor as PW.3 and another witness as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to 21. 
On the other hand, respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary. 
3.4 On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.4,05,000/- with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till its realization and respondent No.2-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of the order. 
3.5 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court NC: 2024:KHC:5384 challenging the impugned judgment and award, seeking enhancement.
4. The main contention of the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation and it has not taken into consideration the avocation, age and the magnitude of the injuries sustained by the claimant due to road traffic accident. The tribunal has not awarded reasonable compensation under other heads also. 
Accordingly, he seeks to allow the appeal preferred by the claimant and seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company submits that the tribunal has rightly awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference. Therefore,
on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal. 
6. Having heard the learned counsel for appellant- claimant and learned counsel for respondent-Insurance NC: 2024:KHC:5384 Company, perused the impugned judgment and award. 
Exs.P1 to P5 are police records, wherein the FIR and charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the offending vehicle. Exs.P6 to P.21 are the medical records, which depicts the expenses incurred by the claimant. The Tribunal has rightly arrived to the conclusion that the negligence is attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle. 
7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income and disability, PW.3-Doctor has opined that there is disability to an extent of 10% to the whole body. However, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 8% to the whole body. The income taken by the tribunal is Rs.11,000/- per month as notional income, no documentary proof is produced before the tribunal to show the income. 
However, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.14,000/- for the accident of the year 2019. Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.14,000/-. The age of NC: 2024:KHC:5384 the claimant was 38 years at the time of accident. The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '15', which does not call for interference. Therefore, the loss of future income due to disability would be Rs.2,01,600/- (Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 15 x 8%) as against Rs.1,58,000/- awarded by the tribunal. 
8. Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, Rs.1,56,000/- is awarded by the tribunal on the basis of actual bills produced by the claimant, which also does not Chandrashekar N Shetty @ Chandrashekar vs Suresh Kumar C on 8 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52045495/
3 call for interference. 
9. The tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- towards food nourishment and miscellaneous expenditure. 
I deem it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.10,000/-. In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.20,000/- under this head. 
10. Towards loss of earning during period of treatment, the tribunal has awarded Rs.11,000/-. In view of enhancement of the income by this Court to NC: 2024:KHC:5384 Rs.14,000/- per month,
the claimant would require atleast three months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities. Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.42,000/- (Rs.14,000/- x 3)
under this head. 
11. Towards pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-, which does not call for interference and the same is retained. 
12. The tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities. I deem it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.10,000/-. In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.30,000/- under this head. 
13. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,99,600/- as against Rs.4,46,000/- as mentioned in the table below: 
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Expenses relating to treatment, 1,56,000-00 hospitalization, medicines, transportation Food nourishment and miscellaneous 20,000-00 expenditure NC: 2024:KHC:5384 Loss of earnings during period of 42,000-00 treatment Loss of future earnings on account of 2,01,600-00 disability Damages for pain, suffering and trauma 50,000-00 as a consequence of the injuries Loss of amenities 30,000-00 TOTAL 4,99,600-00 14. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed-in-part;
ii) The judgment and award dated 25.02.2021 passed by VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (SCCH-5) at Bengaluru in MVC.No.2710/2019 is modified;
iii) The claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.4,99,600/- as against Rs.4,05,000/- awarded by the tribunal;
iv) The interest awarded by the tribunal at the rate of 9% per annum on the compensation amount of Rs.4,05,000/- is left undisturbed. The enhanced Chandrashekar N Shetty @ Chandrashekar vs Suresh Kumar C on 8 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52045495/
4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:5384 compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum;
v) The enhanced compensation amount shall be paid by the respondent within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment;
vi) The compensation amount shall be released in favour of the claimant, upon proper verification.
Sd/-
